summary: Frontend-only UI verification of new /admin/personal-track (PersonalTrackAdmin). Login via test@aurem.dev succeeds. /admin sidebar contains 'Personal Track ops' link (data-testid=admin-nav-personal-track). Clicking navigates to /admin/personal-track. Page eventually renders correctly with heading 'Personal Track Ops', all 4 stat tiles (Drafts=7, Materialized=0, Blocked=0, Pending Downgrades=0), both health cards, and all three empty-state sections ('No blocked drafts', 'No Personal Track projects yet', 'No pending downgrades'). All 6 backend calls returned 200 (draft-summary, blocked-drafts, personal-projects, llm-health, pending-downgrades, dev-users/created-at-health). No console errors, no page errors. HOWEVER, the page shows a full-screen loader for ~30s before rendering because GET /scaffold/admin/llm-health takes ~29-32s and load() uses Promise.allSettled — the loading flag stays true until *all* six promises settle, so the entire admin dashboard is gated on the slowest (non-critical) probe.

minor.issue: Very slow: ~29-32s per request (measured via curl and browser). Returns 200 with fallback active / file_count=0. Not a functional failure, but latency drives the UX issue below.

ui_bugs.issue: Full-screen spinner blocks the entire page for ~30s on first load because load() awaits Promise.allSettled of all six probes before flipping loading=false; llm-health is the slow one (~30s). Users perceive page as hung/blank. Recommend: (a) render the page immediately with per-card skeletons/loading states, or (b) fire llm-health as a separate non-blocking effect, or (c) attach a per-request timeout (e.g. 5s) for llm-health so a slow probe doesn't gate the whole dashboard.

action_items: Decouple loading state from llm-health probe (either non-blocking useEffect for llm-health, per-card skeletons, or short per-request timeout) so the admin dashboard renders in <1s instead of ~30s.
Investigate why /scaffold/admin/llm-health takes ~30s (falls back after a network timeout to some upstream LLM?). Consider caching the probe result server-side for 30-60s.

Optional: verify auth-protection behavior for unauthenticated visits to /admin/personal-track — current behavior is that the page mounts and stays on the spinner (backend returns 401 on the probes) rather than redirecting to /login. Non-admin users still cannot see data, but the UX is a silent spinner. Consider redirecting to /login when probes return 401.
critical_code_review_comments: PersonalTrackAdmin.load(): using Promise.allSettled on 6 probes and only flipping loading=false in the finally block means the whole page is gated on the slowest probe. Prefer per-widget loading states or split fast/slow probes.
override() uses window.prompt() — acceptable for admin tool but not friendly on mobile / accessibility. Non-blocking suggestion.
No explicit admin-role guard in the component — relies purely on backend 401s. If an unauthenticated user hits the route directly, they see a permanent spinner (see action item).

success_rate.frontend: 90% (page renders + all endpoints wired correctly + empty states OK; 1 UX issue: 30s spinner)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Login via POST /api/aurem-dev/auth/login returns {token} (not access_token). /admin sidebar link testid = admin-nav-personal-track. All expected data-testids on the page work once it renders. The one recurring pitfall: waiting less than ~35s after load() causes the page to appear blank/spinning — always use wait_for_selector('[data-testid=pt-tile-drafts]', timeout=50000).
rca of the issue: RCA — 30s blank spinner on /admin/personal-track: load() in PersonalTrackAdmin.jsx does `await Promise.allSettled([...6 api.get(...)])` then flips loading=false in finally. Backend /scaffold/admin/llm-health consistently takes ~29-32s (measured curl 32.55s, browser 29.14s reported in fallback UI). The other 5 probes finish in <200ms. Because allSettled waits for the slowest, users see a full-screen Loader2 for ~30s. Reproduction: login → navigate to /admin/personal-track → observe spinner for ~30s → then full page renders with correct data. Mitigation: split llm-health into an independent, non-blocking effect (or add a Promise.race timeout around it), and/or cache the llm-health probe server-side.
